name: aa_nitrogen_disposal
description: Amino-acid nitrogen disposal hub. Most amino acids transfer their α-amino group to α-ketoglutarate (aminotransferases → glutamate). Glutamate dehydrogenase releases free NH₄⁺; aspartate donates the second N into the urea cycle. Carbon skeletons exit as α-keto acids toward glucogenic or ketogenic fates. Links to existing urea_cycle graph.

references: Berg JM, Tymoczko JL, Stryer L. Biochemistry — Amino Acid Degradation and the Urea Cycle.
Lehninger Principles of Biochemistry — Nitrogen excretion and the urea cycle.

nodes.label: α-Ketoglutarate
nodes.notes: Universal amino-group acceptor for most transaminations.

nodes.label: Glutamate
nodes.notes: Central nitrogen collector in liver (and muscle ALT branch).

nodes.label: α-Keto acid (carbon skeleton)
nodes.notes: Enters TCA / GNG / ketone paths depending on AA identity.

nodes.label: Ammonia (NH₄⁺)
nodes.notes: Toxic; must be detoxified — mainly via urea cycle in liver.

nodes.label: Aspartate
nodes.notes: Second nitrogen donor to urea (via argininosuccinate synthetase).

nodes.label: Urea cycle (see urea_cycle pack)
nodes.notes: Teaching link node — full cycle is modeled in urea_cycle.py.

nodes.label: Glutamine
nodes.notes: Safe N transport form (muscle → gut/kidney/liver); GLS releases NH₄⁺.

edges.notes: Transfers α-amino N; leaves the carbon skeleton as an α-keto acid.
α-KG + amino-N → glutamate. Coupled to AA → α-keto acid.
Oxidative deamination regenerates α-KG and free NH₄⁺.
Glu + OAA ⇌ α-KG + Asp. Feeds the second N into urea.
NH₄⁺ + CO₂ → carbamoyl phosphate. Full topology in urea_cycle pack.
Asp donates the second nitrogen atom of urea.
NH₄⁺ + Glu + ATP → Gln. Safe inter-organ nitrogen transport.
Releases NH₄⁺ for urea (liver) or ammonium excretion (kidney).
